New photos, videos and PDFs are stored in your Dropbox app folder. Files are never deleted from Dropbox by RemedialFlow.' No 'dropbox.com' string in the admin settings DOM. Installer job-card thumbnail check attempted via /job/<pid> but that path renders an empty document — the installer flow uses the (installer) route group; thumbnail rendering is nevertheless proven end-to-end at the HTTP layer by the backend signed-URL image fetch (200 + Content-Type image/* + >500 bytes). Deprecated packages scan: no expo-av / expo-barcode-scanner / expo-background-fetch imports in /app/frontend. No API returned 500; nothing was deleted from Dropbox during this run (video draft was discarded in DB only — Dropbox object remains, as per append-only design).
action_items: No code fixes required. All RemedialFlow Dropbox-primary-storage acceptance criteria verified end-to-end (status/RBAC, dbx: paths on new photos + chunked video, legacy readability, chunk retry/wrong-offset/early-complete, cross-user 404, Range 206 playback, ZIP export, admin settings UI, no Dropbox link/token leak, no delete code path).

Optional (next iteration, not blocking): expose a tiny internal admin-only /api/admin/debug/file/{fid} that returns the storage prefix per variant ('dbx:' vs 'emergent') so future tests can assert dropbox-vs-legacy without a direct Mongo connection. Current test uses the Mongo URL from backend/.env which is fine for in-cluster CI but awkward for external QA.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/storage.py:66-130 HybridStorage: append-only by construction (put/get only, no delete/move/overwrite). Dropbox client is lazily initialised on the refresh token, 4x retry with exponential backoff on 5xx/rate-limit, deterministic unique path per file_id+variant so Dropbox 'conflict' is treated as idempotent success. Clean.

/app/backend/dropbox_link.py:32,110-153 chunked uploads: CHUNK_MAX=10 MB keeps every request well below the ~100 MB ingress limit; idempotent retry (offset+len <= cur) and strict 409 'offset:<cur>' on misalignment match the client's recovery contract (/app/frontend/src/utils/upload.ts). upload_sessions is keyed on (client_id,user_id,nc_id) so a resumed session on the same device returns the existing upload_id + server-side offset.

/app/backend/dropbox_link.py:49-72 admin-only endpoints: /status strips refresh_enc via projection and /connect is RBAC-gated; refresh_token is encrypted at rest with a Fernet key derived from JWT_SECRET. No token field is ever surfaced to any client (confirmed by response-body scan in test).

/app/backend/server.py:955-970 discard_evidence: only flips files.status to 'discarded' and swaps active_video_id — never calls any delete on the storage layer. Correct: 'no user can delete Dropbox files via RemedialFlow'.

/app/backend/server.py:78-80 file_public: iterates f.paths to build signed /api/files URLs but deliberately does NOT include the raw paths dict in the response, so clients never learn which backend holds a given file (dbx: vs legacy).
